summary: Hosted generation adapts the shared DurableRunEngine to Cloudflare persistence and existing product projections. Provider protocol stays in adapters/portable provider modules; this directory does not define another Run domain.

key_files.start.ts: Live HTTP/agent/NodeProcessor admission entrypoint; dispatches through runtime, never calls a blocking adapter.
key_files.runtime.ts: CF adapter binding shared hosted generation policy to D1 journal, Workflow scheduling, R2 broker, provider registry, lifecycle plugins and ProjectRoom publication. video_render staging seals the rendered bytes as the tenant's Project Resource; it never prepares a D1 library Asset.
key_files.adapter.ts: One submit or one status poll per invocation. Tokens are private JSON; completed media contains receipt-backed handles.
key_files.context.ts: Invocation-only reference reads and output broker IO. No Workflow steps, journal mutations, D1 Assets or Canvas publication.
key_files.output.ts: R2 immutable byte/receipt CAS scoped by Project and shared run/slot identity. Primary media and optional provider covers have separate verified receipts.
key_files.publication.ts: Owner and task/output checks, immutable legacy D1 Asset preparation, detached shared Canvas operation; ProjectRoom acknowledges durable append before asset_ref visibility. A remote plugin's uploaded output (projectAsset) is imported as Project Asset updates.assetId on the same fork as the node update, so both land together or not at all. Failures project errorMessage + errorCode. video_render runs go to the room's timeline-render-publication operation instead.
key_files.timeline-render-publication.ts: DO-side (lazily imported) publication of a video_render run onto the raw render node the shared request_timeline_render command creates: imports the stage-sealed Resource as Project Asset taskId (provenance render) and completes it with shared completeTimelineRenderNode in one fork; republish is a no-op; failure is projected only while the run still holds pendingTask. Never reads through Canvas, whose scope excludes Project-Asset renders.
key_files.status.ts: Journal-backed public task status overrides legacy Asset-row hints, including text success and obsolete-target failure.
key_files.recovery.ts: Cron recovery across the exported owner list; due rows are re-scheduled by frozen identity only.
key_files.registry.ts: Supported hosted wire adapters; native switches stay first, then an explicit Worker-safe plugin allowlist routes provider-executor plugins through the shared PluginExecutionPort.
key_files.adapters: Provider translation only. Async services return opaque tokens and never own scheduling. adapters/render.ts calls the shared shared-runtime/render-server protocol (renderTimelineVideo) over renderServerFetch; Node uses the same protocol through its own port.
key_files.params.ts: Compatibility type re-export of shared-runtime generation-params.
key_files.plugin-provider-adapter.ts: Plugin-owned provider routes: builds the same frozen provider values as the Node adapter, binds credentials from the selected hosted account, and calls the in-process PluginExecutionPort.
key_files.plugin-execution: Dynamically imported Cloudflare composition root for first-party in-process plugin modules, their ExecutorContext, and durable invocation replay. Never in Worker startup.
key_files.executable-admission.ts: Canvas custom Action admission: validates the node's frozen pluginBinding, fails plugin_unavailable without a row, claims the node, journals under api-cf:executable, then schedules the existing GenerationWorkflow.
key_files.executable-runtime.ts: Cloudflare composition root for executable Actions: shared DurableRunEngine coordinator, PluginExecutionPort provider, R2 stage and ProjectRoom publication. A remote plugin's media answer (the run's pre-assigned pluginOutputAssetId) is staged by sealing its completed upload session and published as a Project Asset once, keyed by the run.
key_files.executable-binding.ts: Resolve a frozen binding to code-registered first-party execution or the user's per-plugin remote endpoint; first-party ids never use the remote path.
key_files.executable-action-params.ts: Hosted admission/publication view of one frozen executable Action run.
key_files.project-owner.ts: Accountable Project owner lookup used by remote settings and Asset publication.
key_files.official-media.ts: #359 official media/AIGC through gateway-core + ledger: a media run no BYOK account serves is planned on the shared route plan (one gateway_media_job per task), admitted (hold + media-job lease) in beforeGenerate, settled in afterGenerate (delivered units, once) or onFailure (zero, always). Official credentials resolve only for the admitted run that planned them. Guide: apps/docs/guide/gateway-data-plane.md#media-and-aigc.
key_files.media-usage.ts: #359 the one usage writer: quantities a media run asks for/delivers (price book picks the charged units), and one provider_usage_audit row per BYOK run when it ends, unless the adapter recordsProviderUsage (Pika). Adapters never meter.
key_files.official-media.test.ts: The hosted pipeline over migrated node:sqlite D1 with a stub adapter: BYOK->official fallback, hold before the provider, success charged once, failure after acceptance never charged (replays/late success duplicate), refusals, credential custody (plugin store too), BYOK usage backfill.

compatibility: Live GenerationWorkflow uses shared graph and D1/R2 ports while retaining legacy task IDs and D1 Asset/node publication; this is not native Generator Output Commit migration. Timeline renders are the exception: they publish a Project Asset like the browser render path and api-node. A render node without Timeline provenance (sourceTimelineId/sourceTimelineRevisionId) fails publication and is projected failed.
Pre-migration Workflow payloads without a durable identity require owner reconciliation; they are never blindly resubmitted.
Hook completion markers prevent ordinary replay, not exactly-once external billing. Billing integrations must deduplicate by taskId.

Provider failure values use the portable action-sdk/executable-failure subpath. Unit-test aliases resolve both SDK root and subpaths to one source implementation, preserving instanceof across adapters and runtime.
Executable Action runs share the hosted D1 journal, GenerationWorkflow, R2 broker and ProjectRoom publication; they live under owner api-cf:executable.
